targetReport.title: The Local Government Finance Act [CAP. 290 R.E. 2019]
targetReport.publisher: Ministry of Finance and Planning, United Republic of Tanzania
targetReport.description: Tanzania's national statute governing Local Government Authority own-source revenue. Verified via direct PDF download and text extraction. Section 6(1)(u) (urban authorities): "all monies derived from the service levy payable by corporate entities or any person conducting business with business licence at the rate not exceeding 0.3 percent of the turnover net of the value added tax and excise duty" (an equivalent clause for district councils appears at Section 7(1)(y)). Section 31A(1): "Notwithstanding the provisions of this Act, the Tanzania Revenue Authority shall have the obligation to evaluate, assess, collect and account for property rate and advertisement fees for billboards, posters and hoarding" — property rate is listed as an LGA revenue category (Sections 6(1)(o)/7(1)(z)) but its evaluation/assessment/collection was statutorily reassigned to the national Tanzania Revenue Authority, meaning LGAs no longer administer this own-source revenue line themselves.
targetReport.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument (R.E. 2019 = Revised Edition 2019).

The Centre is established as a regional office of the Bank created by the 2014 instrument.

targetReport.title: Agreement on the New Development Bank (Fortaleza, 15 July 2014) and annexed Articles of Agreement
targetReport.publisher: Governments of the Federative Republic of Brazil, the Russian Federation, the Republic of India, the People's Republic of China and the Republic of South Africa
targetReport.description: Foundational treaty establishing the New Development Bank (NDB). Signed in Fortaleza on 15 July 2014 by the five founding BRICS members. Entered into force 3 July 2015 after all five deposited instruments of acceptance/ratification. Russia ratified by Federal Law No. 29-FZ of 8 March 2015. Creates the Bank, sets purpose (mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable development in BRICS and other EMDCs), capital structure (initial authorised USD 100 bn, subscribed USD 50 bn), governance, and membership rules. Continuously cited as the legal basis in every subsequent NDB Annual Report, strategy document, and project approval.

results.basis: Règlement grand-ducal du 20 décembre 1999, Art. 1er: STATEC 'établit chaque mois un indice des prix à la consommation conformément aux dispositions du Règlement (CE) n° 2494/95 du Conseil du 23 octobre 1995 relatif aux indices des prix à la consommation harmonisés' [establishes monthly a consumer price index in accordance with the provisions of Council Regulation (EC) No 2494/95 of 23 October 1995 on harmonised indices of consumer prices]. Same shape as de-destatis-national-accounts -> esa-2010: a binding EU regulation supplies the definitions and methodology a national release conforms to, not figures. eurostat-hicp's own description states it is 'calculated according to a harmonised approach and definitions as laid down in Regulations and Recommendations' -- the same regulatory framework named here. Not extended to lu-statec-ipcn: Art. 1er says the IPCN merely 'se conforme aux mêmes principes et concepts méthodologiques' [conforms to the same methodological principles and concepts] as the IPCH, without itself being subject to Regulation 2494/95 -- a Research.1 §5a 'comparable with' shape, not a documented dependency, so no edge is drawn for the IPCN side.

targetReport.title: Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP)
targetReport.description: Eurostat's own metadata states: 'The Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) gives comparable measures of inflation for the countries and country groups for which it is produced... a set of consumer price indices (CPIs) calculated according to a harmonised approach and definitions as laid down in Regulations and Recommendations. In addition, the HICP provides the official measure of consumer price inflation in the euro area [for] monetary policy purpose[s].' Named directly by Annex XI to the Staff Regulations of Officials of the European Union as the Belgian component of the 'Joint Index' used to calculate the annual update of EU staff remuneration and pensions (Article 1(2)) -- see _dropped.
targetReport.cadence_note: 'The data are disseminated monthly, around the middle of the month that follows the reference month' (Eurostat metadata page, 'Frequency of dissemination'). A flash estimate for the euro area is disseminated even earlier, on or near the last working day of the reference month.

entries.covers: July 2026 HICP (full release, euro area annual inflation)

release_schedule.note: Eurostat's HICP release calendar is set roughly a year in advance and published under 'Euro indicators' (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/news/euro-indicators/release-calendar), which loads dynamically and could not be scraped directly. The confirmed next date (19 Aug 2026, covering July 2026 data) comes from the 'next release' notice on the 31 July 2026 flash-estimate press release. Per the HICP ESMS metadata page, full HICP releases occur monthly, 'usually between 15 and 18 days after the end of the reference month' (except January, released toward end of February for annual weight updates); a separate flash estimate is published on the last working day of the reference month or shortly after.

results.basis: The new MPP pension arrangement is integrated with the Public Service Pension Plan; MPPs therefore become subject to the same PSPP COLA rules once in receipt of pension. The document states: "The new pension plan for MPPs would be integrated with the Public Service Pension Plan (PSPP). MPPs would join the PSPP on the same terms as other members, plus receive an additional supplementary pension benefit."

targetReport.title: Public Service Pension Plan (PSPP) Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) Methodology
targetReport.description: Formal formula for annual COLA applied to PSPP pensions in pay. Escalation factor is calculated from the average Statistics Canada Consumer Price Index over two consecutive 12-month periods ending 30 September. Maximum annual increase 8%; excess carried forward. Applied each January. Primary provincial mechanism that directly indexes a major compensation stream to CPI.
